title: Strangers from Yathrib
hook: The people of Makkah turned him away. A handful of pilgrims from a farming town said yes.

screens.text: **His own city had turned him away.** So at pilgrimage season, he walked from camp to camp, asking visitors to listen. Most didn't. Then a few men from a farming town did.

**A few strangers say yes.** During the **Hajj** season, when tribes came to Makkah, he invited them to Islam. A few men of the Khazraj tribe from Yathrib, a farming town to the north, accepted [IslamQA 11575].
bubbles: Yathrib is the town we now call Madinah. Nobody in Makkah expected help to come from there.

screens.prompt: The next year, about a dozen came back and made a pledge. What did they promise? Pick all that apply.

options.text: Not to steal, commit zina, or kill their children
options.feedback: Yes. The pledge was about how they would live, not only what they believed [Bukhari 18].

options.text: Not to slander anyone, and to obey him in what is good
options.feedback: Yes. Clean speech and doing good together were part of it [Bukhari 18].
Not quite. This first pledge was about faith and character. No fighting was mentioned.

screens.text: **A teacher sent ahead.** He sent Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr back with them to teach the Qur'an. Mus'ab was one of the first Muslims to reach Yathrib, and through him many there accepted Islam [Bukhari 3925; IslamQA 11575].
bubbles: Before any city welcomed the Prophet ﷺ, it welcomed a teacher. The new Muslims of Yathrib learned their faith from one patient person at a time.

screens.text: How a farming town became a home.

events.title: A few say yes
events.text: Some men of Khazraj from Yathrib accept Islam at Hajj [IslamQA 11575].

events.title: The first pledge
events.text: About a dozen pledge faith and good conduct [Bukhari 18; IslamQA 11575].

events.title: Mus'ab teaches
events.text: Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr goes to Yathrib to teach the Qur'an [Bukhari 3925].

events.title: The night pledge
events.text: More than seventy meet him secretly at night and promise to protect him [IslamQA 11575].

events.title: The move
events.text: Muslims begin leaving Makkah for Yathrib.

screens.text: **A secret meeting at night.** The next year, more than seventy came. They met him in the dark at a place called 'Aqabah and promised to protect him if he came to live with them [IslamQA 11575; Yaqeen (Hate)].
bubbles: His uncle al-'Abbas came with him, though, the sources say, he wasn't Muslim yet. Family who don't share your faith can still stand by you [IslamQA 11575].

screens.prompt: You're from Yathrib, at that night meeting. Why does your promise matter so much?

options.text: He'd be leaving his home city and needed people who would truly protect him
options.feedback: Right. They were promising him a new home and their protection. Soon after, he came.

options.text: Because they wanted him to rule their trade
options.feedback: Not quite. The pledge was about faith and protection, not business.

options.text: It didn't matter; he was staying in Makkah
options.feedback: Not quite. This pledge opened the way for him to leave Makkah. That's the next episode.

screens.text: **Your people may be somewhere new.** The city he grew up in said no. Strangers from a town he'd never lived in said yes. If the people you started with don't understand your faith, Allah can open a door you didn't expect.
bubbles: Day 48 talked about Muslims who let you down. Sometimes the welcome comes from a different masjid, a study circle, or one person who becomes your Mus'ab.

screens.situation: Dre's old friends joke about his "new religion" and stopped inviting him out. At a masjid across town, a Saturday study circle keeps saving him a seat. He wonders if it's disloyal to spend more time there.

options.text: Keep showing up to the circle, and stay kind to his old friends
options.feedback: Yes. A new community doesn't cancel old ties. He can be warm to both, and grow where he's welcomed.

options.text: Stop going to the circle so his old friends don't feel replaced
options.feedback: Not quite. He needs people who support his faith. The pilgrims from Yathrib changed everything by saying yes.

options.text: Cut off his old friends completely
options.feedback: Not quite. He can keep kind ties. Even the Prophet's ﷺ uncle, not yet Muslim, stood by him.

chips: Why did people from Yathrib say yes?
My masjid feels cold. Where else can I look?

screens.prompt: Who was a "stranger who said yes" in your own journey to Islam? Who could you be that for?

screens.text: Say yes to one new connection.
steps: Find one Muslim gathering near you: a class, a circle or a meal
Message someone to ask about it, or put it in your calendar

screens.text: Makkah said no, and strangers from a farming town said yes. Your people might be waiting somewhere you haven't looked yet.
Next episode: assassins wait at his door, and his young cousin lies in his bed.

check.prompt: Who did he send to Yathrib to teach the Qur'an?

options.feedback: Right. He was among the first Muslims to arrive there, teaching the Qur'an [Bukhari 3925].
Not quite. Abu Talib had already died. He sent a young Companion, Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr.

check.prompt: What did the more than seventy promise at 'Aqabah?

options.text: To protect him if he came to live with them
options.feedback: Right. It opened the door to his move to Yathrib.

options.text: To bring him their tribe's wealth
options.feedback: Not quite. It was a promise of protection, not money.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- At the Hajj season he invited visiting tribes; a few men of Khazraj from Yathrib (later Madinah) accepted Islam [IslamQA 11575].
- The next year about a dozen ("over ten", IslamQA 11575) came and pledged: to worship nothing besides Allah, not to steal, commit zina, kill their children or slander, and to obey him in good [Bukhari 18]. 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who narrates it, was one of their leaders.
- He sent Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr with them to teach the Qur'an; Mus'ab was among the first to reach Madinah, and many there accepted Islam, among them Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Usayd ibn Hudayr [Bukhari 3925; IslamQA 11575].
- The following year more than seventy came, met him secretly at night at 'Aqabah with his uncle al-'Abbas present (not yet Muslim), and pledged to protect him if he came to them [IslamQA 11575; Yaqeen (How Muhammad Confronted Hate)].

**Likely questions**
- *"How many were at the second pledge?"* Say "more than seventy". A well-known figure in the biographies includes two women, but this track uses only what its sources confirm.
- *"Why did people from Yathrib say yes?"* Keep to the episode: they heard him at Hajj, accepted, and learned from Mus'ab. Don't add tribal-war history unless the convert asks, and then keep it brief and say it comes from the early biographers.
- *"My masjid feels cold. Where else can I look?"* Listen first. Suggest another masjid, a study circle, a convert group, and the mentor; Day 48 covers this.
- *"Was al-'Abbas Muslim?"* Not at that time, according to the early biographers. He's an example of family who protect you without sharing your faith.

**Escalate:** nothing specific.

**Don't**
- Don't give the second-pledge number as an exact count.
- Don't encourage the convert to cut off old friends or family.
sourcesMd:
- [Bukhari 18](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:18) (Sahih): the terms of the pledge, narrated by 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.
- [Bukhari 3925](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3925) (Sahih): Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr among the first to reach Madinah, teaching the Qur'an.
- [IslamQA 11575, *Who Is Muhammad?*](https://islamqa.info/en/answers/11575): Khazraj at Hajj; "over ten" at the first pledge; Mus'ab sent; "more than seventy" at 'Aqabah with al-'Abbas present.
- [Yaqeen Institute, *How Muhammad ﷺ Confronted Hate and Became the Most Influential Person in History*](https://yaqeeninstitute.org/read/paper/how-muhammad-confronted-hate-and-became-the-most-influential-person-in-history): the delegates from Yathrib pledged at the pilgrimage season.
- Fact rows 19.1–19.5 in Seerah Fact-Check Log.
